keywords: circle circles radius diameter circumference chord arc pi centre center
facts: Every point on a circle is the same distance from its centre; that distance is the radius.
The diameter is a line through the centre from edge to edge; it is twice the radius (d = 2r).
The circumference is the distance around the circle: C = 2 × pi × r.
The area of a circle is pi × r × r (pi r squared).
Pi is about 3.14, or 22/7; it is the same for every circle.
A chord joins two points on the circle; an arc is part of the circumference.

scenes.heading: What is a circle?
scenes.subtitle: Every point the same distance from the centre

narration.text: Wheels, coins and clocks are all circles. Let us see what makes a circle.

scenes.heading: Step 1: The parts of a circle

narration.text: Every circle has a centre, the point right in the middle.
The radius goes from the centre to the edge. It is the same in every direction.
The diameter goes right across, through the centre. It is two radii long.
The circumference is the distance all the way around.

scenes.heading: Step 2: From radius to diameter
scenes.problem: A wheel has a radius of 7 cm. What is its diameter?

narration.text: A wheel has a radius of seven centimetres.
The diameter is two times the radius.
Two times seven is fourteen, so the diameter is fourteen centimetres.
A chord joins two points on the circle. The diameter is the longest chord.
An arc is a part of the circumference, like a slice of the edge.
The area is the space inside: pi times r times r.

scenes.heading: Step 3: Circumference with numbers
scenes.problem: Radius 7 cm. Find the circumference (take π = 22/7).

narration.text: Circumference is two times pi times the radius.
Put in pi as twenty-two over seven, and r as seven.
The sevens cancel, leaving two times twenty-two: forty-four centimetres.

scenes.heading: Step 3: Area with numbers
scenes.problem: Radius 7 cm. Find the area (take π = 22/7).

narration.text: The area is pi times r times r.
Put in twenty-two over seven, and seven times seven.
One seven cancels, leaving twenty-two times seven: one hundred fifty-four square centimetres.

scenes.heading: Step 4: Why the area is π r²

narration.text: Cut the circle into many thin slices, like a pizza.
Lay them side by side, pointing up and down in turn.
They make almost a rectangle, r tall and half the circumference long.
Half the circumference is pi r, so the area is pi r times r.

scenes.heading: Quick check
scenes.question: The radius is 5 cm. What is the diameter?

narration.text: Quick check. If the radius is five centimetres, what is the diameter?
Ten centimetres: two times the radius.

scenes.heading: Quick check
scenes.question: Radius 7 cm, π = 22/7. What is the circumference?

narration.text: Quick check. What is the circumference when the radius is seven?
Forty-four centimetres: two times twenty-two over seven times seven.

scenes.heading: Quick check
scenes.question: Radius 7 cm, π = 22/7. What is the area?

narration.text: Quick check. What is the area when the radius is seven?
One hundred fifty-four square centimetres.
